zurds

zurds reads the files R writes with saveRDS(), save() and serialize(), and lazy-load databases, without handing them to R’s deserializer. It can tell you what a file holds, pull out one object, check whether a file is safe to load, and read data-only files with a reader that cannot run code.

readRDS() and load() are all or nothing: to learn what a 2 GB .rda contains, or whether a model file from a colleague carries closures and environments, you have to load all of it, and loading can run code (CVE-2024-27322). zurds walks the file instead, building nothing it was not asked for.

Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

install.packages("zurds")

Or the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zurds")

What is in a file 

library(zurds)
f <- system.file("extdata", "objects.rda", package = "zurds")

rds_toc(f)
#>        name    type      class length     dim size offset risky
#> 1      cars    list data.frame     11 10 x 11 1396     48 FALSE
#> 2   species integer     factor      3    <NA>  133   1467 FALSE
#> 3      grid  double       <NA>      6   2 x 3   95   1620 FALSE
#> 4 summarise closure       <NA>      1    <NA>  132   1740  TRUE

rds_str() summarises any file the way str() does, and rds_info() reads its header.

Is it safe to load? 

rds_scan(system.file("extdata", "promise.rds", package = "zurds"))
#>    path finding detail severity
#> 1 [[2]] promise   <NA> executes

A promise, a closure or bytecode can run code; an environment, a namespace or an external pointer reaches outside the file; ALTREP and S4 classes need their packages. rds_is_safe() is TRUE when the scan finds nothing, and rds_deps() lists the packages a file would need.

Reading data safely 

f <- system.file("extdata", "iris.rds", package = "zurds")
identical(rds_read_data(f), readRDS(f))
#> [1] TRUE

rds_read_data() builds only vectors, lists and their attributes, and refuses everything else. rds_extract() reads one object, element or column without building the rest, and rds_lazyload_toc() and rds_lazyload_extract() do the same for lazy-load databases.

See vignette("safe-reading", package = "zurds") for what the safety guarantee covers and what it does not.
